title: Treat passing tests and helper output as evidence for review, never as acceptance or authority
summary: An automation's own green result is evidence a reviewer should weigh; it is not the act of being accepted. No tool should self-author acceptance, grant authority, or treat its own 'passed' as approval to mutate or bypass a gate. This matters doubly when an LLM writes the tool, because it will happily make a summary 'decide' something.
technique: separate evidence (what a helper returned or a validator proved) from acceptance (stated by an authority or reviewed path). A lesson, overridden lesson, passing validation, or reporter claim informs but does not by itself accept. Absent facts stay absent and are treated as unknown/deny rather than invented approval.

invariants: A green pass is input to review, not the approval itself.
Report what you can prove; add the unresolved case as unknown/for-review rather than a confident guess or acceptance.
Do not grant authority or mutate from within the validating step; record evidence and let the authority path accept.
Absence (no answer, no fixture, no record) denies or goes to review; it never silently becomes an allow.
